name: Scientific Templates
description: Editable starting points for common experimental-biology figures and presentations.

scenes.name: Immunoblot assay workflow
scenes.summary: An editable immunoblot workflow from sample collection and lysis through SDS-PAGE, membrane transfer, antibody probing, signal detection, and one illustrative target/loading-control result.
scenes.biology_note: Shows sample collection and lysis, clarified lysate, total-protein assessment and planned loading, SDS-PAGE, membrane transfer, blocking with primary/secondary antibody probing, signal detection, and one illustrative target/loading-control result.
scenes.limitations: Bands are placeholders, not data. The loading control must be validated for the sample and treatment context. This starter does not establish detector linearity, transfer efficiency, antibody specificity, normalization validity, fold change, statistical significance, biological mechanism, or reproducibility; one blot alone is not a complete quantitative analysis.
scenes.card_summary: Sample preparation, protein separation, antibody probing and signal detection.

scenes.name: Autophagosome–lysosome process
scenes.summary: A qualitative macroautophagy sequence from phagophore formation and selected cargo capture through autophagosome closure, lysosomal fusion, and cargo degradation.
scenes.biology_note: Shows one selected macroautophagy sequence: an LC3-associated phagophore surrounds a SQSTM1/p62-linked cargo example, closes as a double-membrane autophagosome, fuses with a lysosome, and forms an autolysosome where cargo is degraded.
scenes.limitations: Static schematic only; LC3 or SQSTM1/p62 placement does not measure autophagic flux. It does not represent quantitative kinetics, abundance, complete machinery, disease-specific causality, or clinical or therapeutic effects.
scenes.card_summary: Cargo capture, autophagosome closure and lysosomal degradation.

scenes.name: APC–T-cell immune synapse
scenes.summary: Opposing APC and T-cell membranes with antigen recognition, CD28 costimulation, PD-1 checkpoint context, and a bounded signaling handoff.
scenes.biology_note: Orients peptide–MHC/TCR recognition, CD28–B7 costimulation, and PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint context across an APC–T-cell interface, with only LCK–ZAP-70–LAT shown as a proximal signaling handoff.
scenes.limitations: A qualitative orientation schematic, not a complete receptor catalog, quantitative or kinetic pathway, causal analysis, clinical claim, or canonical synapse organization.
scenes.card_summary: Antigen recognition, costimulation and checkpoint signaling across a cell contact.

scenes.name: T-cell activation and PD-1 checkpoint
scenes.summary: Antigen recognition, CD28 co-stimulation, a compact TCR pathway, and one PD-1 inhibitory branch.
scenes.biology_note: Pairs peptide–MHC recognition with CD28–B7 co-stimulation, then shows a deliberately small LCK–ZAP-70–LAT signaling core and PD-1–SHP2 inhibition.
scenes.limitations: A simplified authoring starter, not a complete, quantitative, stoichiometric, temporal, causal, or state-equivalent pathway model.
scenes.card_summary: T-cell activation with a PD-1 checkpoint branch.

scenes.name: Receptor signaling
scenes.summary: Membrane receptor activation with a branched response and an inhibitory regulator.
scenes.card_summary: Ligand binding connects a membrane receptor to downstream signaling.

scenes.name: Tumor microenvironment
scenes.summary: Tumor, immune, stromal, and vascular cells arranged around editable intercellular signals.
scenes.card_summary: Tumor, immune, stromal and vascular relationships in one editable schematic.

scenes.name: Gene regulation and expression
scenes.summary: Chromatin regulation through transcription, RNA processing, nuclear export, and translation.
scenes.card_summary: From chromatin and transcription to RNA and protein.

scenes.name: Culture to quantitative readout
scenes.summary: Cell culture, treatment, plate-based assay, and quantitative dose-response readout.
scenes.card_summary: Culture cells, apply a perturbation and choose complementary readouts.

scenes.name: CRISPR perturbation and validation
scenes.summary: Guide delivery and genome editing followed by PCR, gel, and protein-level validation.
scenes.card_summary: Design a CRISPR perturbation and connect validation to biological readouts.

scenes.name: Microscopy and flow cytometry readout
scenes.summary: One prepared sample branching into fluorescence microscopy and flow-cytometry readouts.
scenes.card_summary: Pair imaging and flow cytometry to characterize a cell population.

scenes.name: Droplet single-cell RNA workflow
scenes.summary: Cell suspension, droplet partitioning and barcoded RNA capture followed by library preparation and sequencing.
scenes.biology_note: Cell suspension, droplet partitioning and barcoded RNA capture followed by library preparation and sequencing.
scenes.limitations: Schematic only; not measured data. Partition occupancy, RNA recovery and cell quality require review.
scenes.card_summary: Droplet capture, molecular barcodes, library preparation and sequencing.

scenes.name: Spatial RNA methods
scenes.summary: Two distinct routes: location-barcoded RNA capture with sequencing, and RNA imaging in fixed tissue.
scenes.biology_note: Two distinct routes: location-barcoded RNA capture with sequencing, and RNA imaging in fixed tissue.
scenes.limitations: Schematic only; not measured data. Capture spots can contain multiple cells; illustrative puncta are not transcript counts.
scenes.card_summary: Compare tissue-associated capture with RNA imaging in place.

scenes.name: RT-qPCR expression workflow
scenes.summary: RNA quality, reverse transcription, amplification, and control-aware expression analysis.
scenes.biology_note: RT-qPCR measures target amplification after RNA is converted to cDNA; interpretation depends on assay performance and validated normalization.
scenes.limitations: Schematic only. No amplification curves, expression values, fold changes, or significance are shown. Validate RNA, primer specificity, efficiency, controls, and reference genes for the experiment.
scenes.card_summary: RNA quality, reverse transcription, amplification, and control-aware expression analysis.

scenes.name: Immunoprecipitation workflow
scenes.summary: Antibody capture of a target from lysate, bead recovery, washing, and downstream analysis.
scenes.biology_note: An antibody enriches its target from a prepared sample; co-immunoprecipitation can recover associated proteins when the complex survives extraction and washing.
scenes.limitations: Schematic only. Recovery is not proof of direct binding. Antibody specificity, lysis conditions, bead background, interaction stability, input, and immunoglobulin-chain interference require experiment-specific controls.
scenes.card_summary: Antibody capture of a target from lysate, bead recovery, washing, and downstream analysis.

scenes.name: Indirect immunofluorescence workflow
scenes.summary: Fixed-cell labeling with a target-specific primary antibody and fluorophore-linked secondary antibody.
scenes.biology_note: The primary antibody recognizes the selected target; a fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibody binds the primary antibody for imaging.
scenes.limitations: Schematic only. Localization and signal are not data. Fixation, permeabilization, antibody specificity, fluorophore cross-reactivity, spectral bleed-through, and imaging settings require validation; include appropriate negative controls.
scenes.card_summary: Fixed-cell labeling with a target-specific primary antibody and fluorophore-linked secondary antibody.

scenes.name: Sandwich ELISA workflow
scenes.summary: Capture antibody, sample antigen, detection antibody, enzyme signal, and calibrated readout.
scenes.biology_note: Two antibodies recognize distinct epitopes of an analyte; an enzyme-linked detection system produces a measurable signal for comparison with standards.
scenes.limitations: Schematic only. No standard curve or concentrations are supplied. Antibody pairing, matrix effects, cross-reactivity, sample dilution, calibration range, and signal saturation must be assessed for the analyte and sample type.
scenes.card_summary: Capture antibody, sample antigen, detection antibody, enzyme signal, and calibrated readout.

scenes.name: Wound-closure assay workflow
scenes.summary: Create a cell-free gap, image matched fields over time, and quantify gap closure.
scenes.biology_note: A gap in a confluent cell layer can be followed by microscopy to assess collective movement into the cleared area.
scenes.limitations: In vitro gap closure does not by itself isolate migration from proliferation, survival, or changes in cell spreading. Standardize gap geometry, image positions, and timing; interpret in the context of model and controls.
scenes.card_summary: Create a cell-free gap, image matched fields over time, and quantify gap closure.

scenes.name: Epithelial barrier Transwell assay
scenes.summary: Grow a polarized epithelial layer on a porous insert and pair electrical and tracer-flux readouts.
scenes.biology_note: An epithelial monolayer separates apical and basolateral compartments; TEER reports ionic conductance while tracer passage measures permeability to the chosen tracer.
scenes.limitations: The two readouts are complementary and not interchangeable. TEER does not measure macromolecule flux; tracer results depend on tracer size, sampling, membrane, model, and assay conditions. A Transwell is an in-vitro model, not an intact organ barrier.
scenes.card_summary: Grow a polarized epithelial layer on a porous insert and pair electrical and tracer-flux readouts.

scenes.name: Chemical synaptic transmission
scenes.summary: Calcium-dependent vesicle release across a chemical synapse, with generic postsynaptic receptors.
scenes.biology_note: At a canonical chemical synapse, presynaptic depolarization promotes calcium-dependent vesicle fusion; released transmitter crosses the cleft and activates postsynaptic receptors.
scenes.limitations: A generalized schematic, not a specific neuron, transmitter, receptor subtype, or measured synaptic response. Release probability, receptor kinetics, short-term plasticity, cotransmission, and clearance mechanisms vary by synapse.
scenes.card_summary: Calcium-dependent vesicle release across a chemical synapse, with generic postsynaptic receptors.

scenes.name: Angiogenic sprouting
scenes.summary: An endothelial sprout near local VEGF cues, with parent vessel, leading tips and neighboring cells.
scenes.biology_note: Endothelial tip cells extend toward proangiogenic cues while neighboring stalk cells support sprout extension; VEGF and DLL4–Notch signaling contribute to tip–stalk patterning.
scenes.limitations: A qualitative spatial schematic, not a universal sequence or measured outcome. Lumen formation and blood flow are not shown. Tip–stalk states are dynamic; matrix, flow, tissue context, VEGF presentation, and signaling can alter sprout behavior and branching.
scenes.card_summary: An endothelial sprout near local VEGF cues, with parent vessel, leading tips and neighboring cells.
